DLI DLPT TRAINER PROJECT · CONTENT REVIEW

Authentic Russian listening

Six radio excerpts. Seventeen questions. Original voices, published timed transcripts, and evidence for every answer.

Draft for teacher review. Files passed full decoding checks. Sound clarity and exact transcript agreement have not been independently auditioned here. The level targets come from the transcripts; overall listening levels remain unset.

Listen before revealing the transcript. Audio is embedded, so this file works offline. Answers are included for review; this is not a secure diagnostic test.

CLIP 1 · 2014-03-01

Аделина Сотникова

Sport / self-description

17.7 secTranscript target 1+≈172.5 caption words/min

Normal-speed original speech. Overall listening level and transcript accuracy await auditory review.

1.1. How does the speaker contrast her everyday self with her experience on the ice?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: B · The answer combines both sides of the contrast; it does not require knowing who the athlete is.

  • A: This reverses the everyday description and does not match the image of a queen on the ice.
  • B: Quiet, modest, and calm contrast with feeling like a queen in her own domain.
  • C: She explicitly says she feels different when she goes onto the ice.
  • D: The passage places the reserved description in everyday life and a sense of ownership on the ice.

Evidence: 00:00.00–00:02.92, 00:02.96–00:06.11, 00:06.14–00:08.76, 00:08.78–00:11.73

1.2. How does she describe herself in ordinary life?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: D · This lower-demand item checks a concrete description rather than knowledge of skating.

  • A: These traits are not her stated everyday self-description.
  • B: She instead calls herself quiet and calm.
  • C: Neither trait is stated; quiet does not mean anxious.
  • D: These directly paraphrase тихая, скромная, спокойная.

Evidence: 00:02.96–00:06.11

Show timed transcript and level rationale

Familiar adjectives and an explicit contrast between daily life and performing. Repeated я чувствую себя supports comprehension; the figurative description raises the second item’s demand.

Review focus: Check the fast delivery suggested by the caption-based pace. Do not test the unusual поделю лед phrase without confirming the sound and interpretation. Two questions are enough for this short, narrow excerpt.

00:00.00–00:02.92 На льду я чувствую себя по-другому, чем в жизни.

00:02.96–00:06.11 В жизни я такая тихая, скромная, спокойная девочка,

00:06.14–00:08.76 а, когда я выхожу на лед, я чувствую себя совсем другой.

00:08.78–00:11.73 Я чувствую себя, можно сказать, королевой на льду, потому что

00:11.78–00:13.19 я никогда не…

00:13.26–00:15.70 поделю лед, потому что это уже моё,

00:15.74–00:17.79 это другие ощущения.

CLIP 2 · 2014-07-26

Дмитрий Шпаро

Creative work / thinking habits

32.1 secTranscript target 2≈129.0 caption words/min

Normal-speed original speech. Overall listening level and transcript accuracy await auditory review.

2.1. What similarity does the speaker draw between writing and proving theorems?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: A · Follow the comparison introduced by похоже на то, как; it concerns a mental process, not a shared workplace.

  • A: He links thinking, recording, and repeated correction in writing to his earlier theorem work.
  • B: He recalls proving theorems on public transport and composing sentences at bedtime.
  • C: No copying or external model is described.
  • D: He says he writes a lot and that the thinking process continues.

Evidence: 00:00.00–00:05.43, 00:07.80–00:12.41, 00:12.43–00:17.78, 00:18.77–00:21.41

2.2. What does he describe doing as he goes to bed?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: C · Distinguish mentally composing sentences now from writing them down later.

  • A: He is forming sentences for the following morning, not reading a completed text.
  • B: The theorem example concerns his earlier activity; this final example concerns sentences.
  • C: He forms sentences at bedtime and hopes to write them the next morning if he remembers.
  • D: No collaborator is mentioned.

Evidence: 00:26.38–00:30.10, 00:30.14–00:32.09

2.3. What qualification does he place on writing those sentences the next morning?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: B · A plan qualified by memory and effort is not a guaranteed result.

  • A: The metro belongs to the earlier theorem example.
  • B: This preserves both если не забуду and постараюсь.
  • C: The conditional and the verb of trying rule out certainty.
  • D: No such check is mentioned.

Evidence: 00:30.14–00:32.09

Show timed transcript and level rationale

A connected personal explanation compares writing with mathematical problem-solving and ends with a conditional intention. Repetitions and embedded clauses require following an unfinished spoken thought.

Review focus: Confirm that the listener can follow the long opening sentence at natural speed. Knowledge of how to prove a theorem is unnecessary; the comparison is stated.

00:00.00–00:05.43 Я все-таки много пишу, и вот когда я пишу,

00:05.45–00:07.76 когда я занимаюсь творчеством,

00:07.80–00:12.41 связанным с тем, что ты мыслишь и что-то такое записываешь,

00:12.43–00:17.78 а потом это исправляешь, исправляешь, исправляешь, исправляешь…

00:18.77–00:21.41 И это очень похоже на то, как я доказывал теоремы.

00:21.53–00:26.35 Я доказывал теоремы, там, в трамвае, в метро, и сейчас всё это продолжается.

00:26.38–00:30.10 Я ложусь спать и составляю те предложения, которые на следующее утро,

00:30.14–00:32.09 если не забуду, постараюсь написать.

CLIP 3 · 2014-08-23

Анатолий Засов

Science / childhood curiosity

30.8 secTranscript target 2≈134.4 caption words/min

Normal-speed original speech. Overall listening level and transcript accuracy await auditory review.

3.1. What initially draws children toward astronomy in the speaker’s account?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: A · The starting point is curiosity about observed phenomena, not formal study or a career plan.

  • A: The opening connects exposure to astronomical phenomena with wanting to know what they are.
  • B: The speaker says adults generally cannot answer their questions.
  • C: Practical concerns appear later as competing interests, not the initial attraction.
  • D: No memorization requirement is described.

Evidence: 00:00.00–00:02.69, 00:02.71–00:04.83, 00:05.32–00:08.22

3.2. What reasons does he give for interest in astronomy fading?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: D · The correct choice retains the alternatives and avoids treating either cause as universal.

  • A: The excerpt begins with unanswered questions, not complete explanations.
  • B: The explanation concerns social and personal interests, not visibility.
  • C: No admission rule or age restriction is mentioned.
  • D: The two alternatives follow либо ... либо.

Evidence: 00:10.77–00:15.24, 00:15.27–00:20.77, 00:23.88–00:26.84

3.3. What does the speaker emphasize at the end?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: C · The final contrast prevents an overly pessimistic interpretation of the earlier generalization.

  • A: Любителей means enthusiasts; the conclusion is not limited to professionals.
  • B: This contradicts the closing statement that there have always been many enthusiasts.
  • C: The final Но qualifies the preceding account of fading curiosity.
  • D: No such improvement is stated.

Evidence: 00:26.88–00:30.79

Show timed transcript and level rationale

The speaker explains a familiar social process using abstract vocabulary, alternative causes, and a qualifying conclusion. No astronomy facts are needed.

Review focus: Review whether the abstract vocabulary pushes the clip toward 2+ for the target group. The question about lost interest should preserve the alternatives rather than assert both occur in every case.

00:00.00–00:02.69 Люди с детства сталкиваются с астрономическими явлениями,

00:02.71–00:04.83 и им интересно понять, что это такое.

00:05.32–00:08.22 А взрослые, как правило, не могут ответить на их вопросы.

00:08.27–00:10.51 Тогда начинают искать, начинают интересоваться.

00:10.77–00:15.24 А потом со временем либо взрослые гасят всякую любознательность,

00:15.27–00:20.77 либо другие интересы настолько перебивают, что уже люди забывают,

00:20.79–00:23.84 что мы часть большого мира, большой Вселенной,

00:23.88–00:26.84 и уже занимаются более прагматичными вещами.

00:26.88–00:30.79 Но любителей-то астрономии всегда много и было, и есть.

CLIP 4 · 2012-10-01

Александр Лазуткин

Spaceflight / response to danger

38.0 secTranscript target 2≈148.4 caption words/min

Normal-speed original speech. Overall listening level and transcript accuracy await auditory review.

4.1. When does the speaker say fear can become prominent?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: B · Track the shift from immediate action to later reflection rather than attaching fear to the opening hypothetical alone.

  • A: He says he acts during the emergency without thinking about how dangerous it is.
  • B: The later reflection follows the urgent response and the situation settling down.
  • C: No outside explanation is required in his account.
  • D: The opening is hypothetical; the main example concerns reflection after emergencies.

Evidence: 00:16.52–00:21.24, 00:25.20–00:28.31, 00:28.92–00:31.97

4.2. What does he describe doing during an emergency?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: A · The item tests the named actions, not technical knowledge of spacecraft repairs.

  • A: These are the two concrete responses he names.
  • B: He emphasizes acting without dwelling on the danger.
  • C: No such division of responsibility is described.
  • D: Reflection is described as following action, not preceding it.

Evidence: 00:16.52–00:21.24, 00:21.54–00:24.54

4.3. What is implied by the final thought that, had events gone differently, he might no longer be thinking?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: D · The phrase is indirect. The context supports possible death, not a specific injury or a claim that the actual event was fatal.

  • A: The counterfactual concerns what could have happened during the dangerous event, not later memory.
  • B: He never makes that causal claim.
  • C: The passage does not state a future decision of that kind.
  • D: The euphemistic ending follows reflection on a dangerous emergency and supports this limited inference.

Evidence: 00:28.92–00:31.97, 00:31.99–00:34.78, 00:34.81–00:38.06

Show timed transcript and level rationale

A concrete account of emergency action is contrasted with later emotional processing. Hypotheticals, false starts, and the elliptical ending increase the inference demand.

Review focus: Check that the fire/collision references and the final counterfactual are intelligible. Keep the inference narrow: he fears a fatal alternative, without specifying an accident outcome beyond what he says.

00:00.00–00:03.51 Если ты начнёшь осознавать степень опасности, ты подумаешь:

00:03.53–00:05.71 а вообще мне стоит лететь туда или не стоит,

00:05.73–00:07.21 стоит так делать или не стоит.

00:07.25–00:09.97 Допустим, когда у нас какие-то там ситуации были страшные,

00:09.99–00:12.59 тот же пожар или столкновение со станцией,

00:14.45–00:16.47 когда наступал момент,

00:16.52–00:21.24 то там кидаешься пожар тушить — ты даже не думаешь, насколько это опасно —

00:21.54–00:24.54 или дырочку закрываешь.

00:25.20–00:28.31 А потом, когда ты осмысливаешь ситуацию,

00:28.92–00:31.97 уже вроде всё улеглось, и тебе становится потом страшно,

00:31.99–00:34.78 думаешь: ёлки-палки, вот если бы я бы вот...

00:34.81–00:38.06 по-другому пошло бы всё, то я бы уже, может быть, и не думал бы.

CLIP 5 · 2009-12-01

Андрис Лиепа

Arts / family expectations

39.8 secTranscript target 2+≈120.7 caption words/min

Normal-speed original speech. Overall listening level and transcript accuracy await auditory review.

5.1. Why does he say he tried to give more than an ordinary effort?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: C · Connect the exaggerated percentage to the reason he gives, rather than treating it as a measurable workload.

  • A: He describes their achievements and his wish to meet the family standard, not discouragement.
  • B: The percentage is rhetorical effort, not a literal work schedule.
  • C: The descriptions of his parents lead directly to the need to match the family’s creative level.
  • D: That general claim is not made.

Evidence: 00:00.00–00:03.95, 00:04.18–00:06.72, 00:07.63–00:09.80, 00:09.85–00:14.27, 00:14.32–00:18.52, 00:18.55–00:21.05

5.2. In this context, what idea is expressed by the saying that “nature rests on the children”?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: B · Use the surrounding account of a talented family to interpret the figurative expression.

  • A: The phrase is not a literal statement about sleep or workload.
  • B: The family’s artistic achievements and pressure to live up to them establish the intended meaning.
  • C: Neither environment nor outdoor life is discussed.
  • D: The saying concerns talent across generations, not decision-making autonomy.

Evidence: 00:07.63–00:09.80, 00:09.85–00:14.27, 00:14.32–00:18.52, 00:18.55–00:21.05, 00:21.30–00:24.60

5.3. What reaction from observers does he find gratifying?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: D · Track the negative qualification не совсем правильное instead of assuming that quoting a saying endorses it.

  • A: No such recommendation is reported.
  • B: The parents’ achievements are not dismissed.
  • C: The concluding qualification says the saying does not quite fit this family.
  • D: This paraphrases the reported view that the saying is not quite right for his family.

Evidence: 00:28.96–00:30.78, 00:30.83–00:34.77, 00:34.83–00:39.84

Show timed transcript and level rationale

The account moves from concrete parental occupations to family expectations and an idiomatic saying whose applicability is challenged. This is a stretch selection rather than an easy biographical clip.

Review focus: Listen for whether the proverb and the final qualification are clear. The proverb’s meaning must be inferred from this family context; do not require prior knowledge of the speaker’s biography.

00:04.18–00:06.72 Я понимал, что родился не в простой семье.

00:07.63–00:09.80 Мама – актриса замечательная драматическая.

00:09.85–00:14.27 Папа – величайший танцовщик 20 века.

00:14.32–00:18.52 И, конечно, надо было как-то соответствовать уровню

00:18.55–00:21.05 творческого какого-то потенциала семьи.

00:21.30–00:24.60 И часто говорят, что природа на детях отдыхает.

00:24.64–00:28.36 И это очень часто в нашей семье звучало.

00:28.96–00:30.78 И сейчас приятные какие-то впечатления

00:30.83–00:34.77 от тех людей, которые смотрят за нами, и видят, и говорят,

00:34.83–00:39.84 что это изречение не совсем правильное в формате Вашей семьи.

CLIP 6 · 2008-01-30

Дарья Донцова

Literature / readers’ expectations

37.5 secTranscript target 2+≈134.3 caption words/min

Normal-speed original speech. Overall listening level and transcript accuracy await auditory review.

6.1. What is the main point of the speaker’s response?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: A · The examples support a principle about appropriate expectations, not a rejection of other genres.

  • A: She distinguishes genres and concludes that readers should understand why they pick up a particular book.
  • B: She uses those expectations as reasons certain readers should not choose her books.
  • C: She recognizes different genres rather than proposing that one replace another.
  • D: Her criticism targets a particular kind of question, not all questions about writing.

Evidence: 00:06.86–00:09.86, 00:09.89–00:12.03, 00:12.23–00:14.52, 00:14.55–00:20.48, 00:34.10–00:37.56

6.2. What does she advise someone seeking geographical knowledge from a book?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: C · Understand the negative recommendation within its stated purpose; it is not a claim that nobody should read her.

  • A: She explicitly says not to read her for that purpose.
  • B: No such reading sequence is recommended.
  • C: The conditional example ends with не читайте госпожу Донцову.
  • D: She does not recommend replacing reading with an interview.

Evidence: 00:20.52–00:24.22, 00:24.25–00:26.63

6.3. Why, in her account, do Western journalists avoid the particular disparaging question she mentions?
Show answer and reasoning

Answer: B · This is the speaker’s characterization of journalists. The item does not assert it as an independently established cultural fact.

  • A: She credits them with understanding genre distinctions, not ignorance of a genre.
  • B: Her Потому что explanation connects their behavior to recognizing genres and their conditions.
  • C: This reverses her explanation of genre differences.
  • D: Geography is a later example of a reader’s purpose, not an explanation of journalists’ behavior.

Evidence: 00:04.10–00:06.62, 00:06.86–00:09.86, 00:09.89–00:12.03, 00:12.23–00:14.52

Show timed transcript and level rationale

An argumentative answer distinguishes genres and uses ironic recommendations and colloquial wording. Understanding the speaker’s position is more demanding than recognizing the listed genres.

Review focus: The source includes the colloquial disparaging phrase паршивые дюдики and the rhetorical что делать. Neither should become an isolated vocabulary test. Confirm delivery and nuance by listening before approval.

00:00.00–00:04.05 Вопрос по поводу того, не противно ли Вам писать паршивые дюдики,

00:04.10–00:06.62 задают только журналисты в России.

00:06.86–00:09.86 Потому что западные журналисты как-то очень хорошо понимают,

00:09.89–00:12.03 что литература состоит из жанров.

00:12.23–00:14.52 И в каждом жанре есть свои условия.

00:14.55–00:20.48 Есть детектив, есть экшн, есть, предположим, философский роман.

00:20.52–00:24.22 Если Вы хотите узнать какие-нибудь знания по географии —

00:24.25–00:26.63 бога ради, не читайте госпожу Донцову.

00:26.73–00:31.51 Если Вы хотите получить ответ на сакральный вопрос: что делать?

00:31.54–00:34.05 Ну, тоже я не для Вас.

00:34.10–00:37.56 Надо понимать, для чего ты берёшь какую книгу в руки.
